title: He grew (Luke 2:41–52)
hook: Jesus advanced in wisdom and age and grace

segments.voice: Yesterday, Simeon held the child in the Temple and asked to be let go in peace. Your line was in peace. Today ends the week.

Every parent's nightmare, in five verses. Every year Mary and Joseph go up to Jerusalem for the Passover, and when Jesus is twelve they go as usual. The feast ends. They start home with a company of relatives and neighbors, thinking he's somewhere among them. A whole day's walk later, they look for him. He isn't there. They turn back and search. One day. Two days. Luke says it was after three days that they found him.
screen: `TWELVE YEARS OLD, AT THE PASSOVER.` → `A DAY'S WALK BEFORE THEY NOTICE.` → `THREE DAYS OF SEARCHING.`

segments.voice: He's in the Temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking them questions, and everyone is astonished at his understanding and his answers. His parents are astonished too, but not in the same way. Mary speaks first, in the Douay-Rheims: "Son, why hast thou done so to us? behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." His answer is the first thing Jesus says in Luke's Gospel: "How is it that you sought me? did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?" The Greek is short and open, literally in the things of my Father: my Father's business, or my Father's house. Translations go both ways. And Luke says plainly: they understood not the word. Then he goes down with them to Nazareth, and is subject to them. The boy who knows who his Father is goes home and does what his parents say. Then Luke's summary: "And Jesus advanced in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men." The Greek for age, helikia, can also mean stature; the King James says stature, the Douay says age, and both are in it. The Church teaches that the Son of God, being truly human, truly grew, in human knowledge as well as in years. Catholics pray this scene as the fifth Joyful Mystery. After this, Luke says nothing more about him until he's a grown man. That closes the week, and Luke's first two chapters: an orderly account, Zachary's silence, the Ave, the Benedictus, Bethlehem, Simeon, and a boy who grew.
screen: `FOUND AMONG THE TEACHERS.` · `MY FATHER'S BUSINESS, OR HOUSE?` · `HE WENT DOWN, AND WAS SUBJECT TO THEM.` · `HELIKIA: AGE, AND STATURE.` · then, large: `JESUS ADVANCED IN WISDOM, AND AGE, AND GRACE.`

segments.voice: Think back to yourself a year ago, or five, and take Luke's three words one at a time: wisdom, something you understand better now; age, the years and the body that carried you here; grace, a way you've been given more than you earned. Don't grade yourself; just notice the growth, even if it's small, even if it came through something hard. If you pray, thank God for it.
He grew. Luke's words about the boy Jesus after the Temple: he advanced in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men. Today's word.
Your line: growing is holy. Even the Son of God grew. That's a week, and day four hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: Catholics pray the finding of Jesus in the Temple as the fifth Joyful Mystery of the rosary, and hear this Gospel on the feast of the Holy Family after Christmas.

chat.who: a friend who's a new parent
chat.says: Did Jesus actually have to grow up and learn things, like any kid?
options: Luke says he advanced in wisdom, age and grace; the Church says he truly grew.
Luke says he stayed in the Temple and grew up among the teachers there.
Luke says he grew up in Bethlehem, learning from the shepherds.
chat.meaning: After the Temple, Jesus went home and was subject to his parents, and advanced in wisdom, age and grace. Being truly human, he truly grew.

Passover.meaning: the Jewish feast Mary and Joseph kept in Jerusalem every year

Joyful Mystery.meaning: one of the rosary's scenes from Jesus's early life

Nazareth.meaning: the town where Jesus grew up
